clue.text: Breeding-ground for dust, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word dust may be read in another order

explanation.surface: Somewhere that dust breeds, like a neglected corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Platform for the last carriage only?

definitions.text: Platform for the last carriage only?

parts.words: Platform for the last carriage only?
parts.note: not a railway platform for the final coach but a stand that carries someone on their final journey

explanation.surface: A railway platform reserved for the rear coach of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin rests on this stand before a funeral, the last carriage anyone gets.

clue.text: Puncture? Jack required on street

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the street comes first

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A flat tyre needs a jack, out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and AB are both sailors. 'on' puts AB beneath ST in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to pierce, making a puncture.

clue.text: Story of bar set up inside fence

indicators.note: inside places the turned word within the fence word

parts.note: a pale is a fence or paling

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word bar is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale about a bar built within a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'set up' means read upwards, so the bar word is reversed before going 'inside' the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale or allegory.

clue.text: Did Figaro work in such close harmony?

definitions.text: Did Figaro work in such close harmony?

parts.words: Did Figaro work in such close harmony?
parts.note: Figaro is the famous barber of Seville, so his workplace would be a hairdressing shop, and close harmony is a style of unaccompanied singing

explanation.surface: Asking whether an opera character sang his part in tight harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a style of close-harmony singing, and also where a barber like Figaro works.

clue.text: Damaging tapestries is a naughty act

indicators.note: damaging the word tapestries pulls its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Ruining wall hangings is bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaging' rearranges TAPESTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque routine of undressing slowly is a risqué performance.

clue.text: Finish in gear, perhaps, when winning

parts.note: to finish is to end

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of in gear may be reordered

explanation.surface: A driver ends up in gear while winning a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like victory but means charming; 'perhaps' signals the rearrangement of 'in gear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning here means charming or attractive, as in a winning smile.

clue.text: Playwright has upset women

indicators.note: upset tells you the word has is knocked into another order

explanation.surface: A dramatist has offended the women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals a rearrangement of 'has'; W for women is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of Pygmalion.

clue.text: This resort, paradoxically, is in the north, right?

definitions.text: This resort, paradoxically, is in the north, right?

parts.words: This resort, paradoxically, is in the north, right?
parts.note: a seaside town whose name begins with the opposite compass point to its location, and whose second half means left rather than right

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a holiday town is really in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHPORT is a seaside resort in north-west England; on a ship, port is left, not right.
explanation.definitionFit: Southport is a Merseyside seaside town, a resort despite its southerly name.

clue.text: Local target of a river authority?

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a board is a governing body or authority

explanation.surface: A body that runs a river has some goal.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British pub, where darts is played; the Dart is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts players in a pub aim at this round board.

clue.text: Old pot in a bag

parts.note: pot as cannabis, for which an old slang name is the same as a drink often sold in sachets

explanation.surface: Some cannabis stashed in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink comes in bags, and the same word was old slang for marijuana.

clue.text: Boss of aircraft that does not take off?

indicators.note: take off tells you to remove a letter, here the opening J

parts.note: a jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large airliner

explanation.surface: The head of an airline whose plane stays grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' removes the J of JUMBO; the joke is that the plane does not take off but its letter does.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the raised central knob or boss of a shield.

clue.text: Swallow in the attic

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words the attic

explanation.surface: A swallow nesting in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow looks like the bird, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to consume it.

clue.text: Criticize a bank-official, say, with a cigar

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk who handles cash

explanation.surface: Attack a bank clerk who is smoking a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes TELLER, as pronounced, give TELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar.

clue.text: Jane Austen's faith in the novel?

definitions.text: Jane Austen's faith in the novel?

parts.words: Jane Austen's faith in the novel?
parts.note: the word for a belief or creed is also the title of one of Austen's books

explanation.surface: Asking about Austen's belief in fiction as a form.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasion is Austen's last completed novel, and a persuasion is a religious belief.

clue.text: Couple with a very recent licence?

definitions.text: Couple with a very recent licence?

parts.words: Couple with a very recent licence?
parts.note: not a pair of new drivers but a pair who have only just got a marriage licence

explanation.surface: A pair who have just passed their driving test.
explanation.definitionFit: A just-married pair has only recently obtained its marriage licence.

clue.text: Like the work of 5,soon upset in test

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: upset knocks the letters of soon out of order

explanation.surface: A job described as soon to be overturned in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 points to 5-down, BARBERSHOP. 'upset' rearranges SOON into ONSO, which goes 'in' TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to hairdressing, the trade of a barber.

clue.text: Injury put in hospital wing?

parts.note: a wing of a building or organisation is an arm

explanation.surface: A patient with an injury admitted to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or hurt done to someone.

clue.text: Design a study

definitions.meaning: a design is a plan or sketch
an artist's study is a preliminary sketch

explanation.definitionFit: A drawing is a sketched plan, and an artist's preparatory sketch is called a study.

clue.text: Paul sent him a letter-it came back full of holes

indicators.note: came back tells you to read the word it backwards

parts.note: taken as written
mothy means moth-eaten, riddled with holes

explanation.surface: A letter returned shredded by moths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns IT into TI. St Paul wrote two epistles to his companion of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two New Testament epistles from Paul are addressed to this disciple.

clue.text: Hearty partner takes much on

parts.note: a mate is a partner
a lot means much

explanation.surface: A cheerful companion takes on a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' is a noun here: an old name for a sailor ('me hearties').
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang for a sailor, as is the noun hearty.

clue.text: Wife battered in front of the kids

definitions.text: Wife battered in front of the kids

parts.words: Wife battered in front of the kids
parts.note: the puppet show where Mr Punch beats his wife before an audience of children

explanation.surface: A grim scene of domestic violence witnessed by children.
explanation.walkthrough: In Punch and Judy, a traditional British seaside puppet show, Punch beats his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch's wife is the puppet beaten in the seaside show watched by children.

clue.text: This butterfly could make a painter go wild

indicators.note: going wild throws the letters of painter go into disorder

explanation.surface: A butterfly so striking it would drive an artist mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges PAINTER GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a white butterfly whose male has orange wingtips.

clue.text: Greek letter chewed up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ate is a past form of eat, and food is chewed

explanation.surface: A Greek character torn to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ATE into ETA in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Battle is bloody in retreat

indicators.note: a retreat goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: raw meat is bloody

explanation.surface: A bloody battle with an army retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: War is armed conflict, a battle on a large scale.

clue.text: Man, for example, lies about

indicators.note: about tells you to turn the letters of lies around

explanation.surface: A man telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea; 'about' rearranges LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: One who does not mind cold sheets under him

definitions.text: One who does not mind cold sheets under him

parts.words: One who does not mind cold sheets under him
parts.note: not someone in a chilly bed but a person gliding over frozen sheets

explanation.surface: A hardy sleeper unbothered by an unheated bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater glides over a frozen sheet of water.

clue.text: Preserve that castle!

definitions.meaning: to preserve is to retain or hold on to
the strongest central tower of a castle

explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to preserve, and a keep is a castle's main tower.

clue.text: David Copperfield's jog?

definitions.meaning: the pet name his great-aunt Betsey gives the hero of the Dickens novel
a jog is a gentle run

explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a jog, and Trot is the nickname his aunt gives David Copperfield.

clue.text: Animal on its back in the long grass

indicators.note: lying on its back turns the word upside down, read upwards in a down answer

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature lying on its back in tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on its back' turns DEER into REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reed is a tall grass growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Shadows 24.for example

definitions.meaning: to shadow someone is to follow them closely
24 is ISLE, and the Isle of this name is in east London

explanation.definitionFit: To dog is to tail someone, and the Isle of Dogs is a district of East London.

clue.text: Free insurance that may protect Windsor?

parts.note: loose means free
cover is insurance protection

explanation.surface: Free insurance protecting the royal castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor suggests the castle, but a Windsor is a wooden chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable fabric slipcover protects a chair such as a Windsor.
